summary: The note surveys startups applying blockchain beyond cryptocurrency, in supply chain, cybersecurity, real estate, healthcare, energy, intellectual property, education and voting. Each sector is illustrated by a startup founded in late 2023 that uses blockchain's secure, transparent, tamper-proof ledger. It closes with an investment case, noting the need for due diligence and that these startups rely on real products rather than token speculation.
one_line: Blockchain startups founded in late 2023 are applying decentralized ledgers to supply chains, security, real estate, healthcare, energy, IP, education and voting.
key_facts: Blockchain is a decentralized digital ledger that records transactions across multiple computers so they cannot be altered retroactively.
ChainTraced, founded by Alice Roberts and Raj Patel on September 15, 2023, uses blockchain to track products from manufacture to delivery in real-time.
ShieldBlock, established by Max Johnson and Li Wei on October 1, 2023, builds blockchain-based decentralized identity verification systems.
PropChain, launched by Sarah Gomez and Akash Singh in November 2023, streamlines contracts and record-keeping to reduce the time and cost of real estate transactions.
MedRec, founded by health IT experts led by Laura Whitmore in late September 2023, secures medical records and lets patients control their healthcare data while preserving privacy.
EnergyBlock, co-founded by Pedro Gonzales and Hina Rizvi on December 5, 2023, enables peer-to-peer energy trading that bypasses traditional grids and suppliers.
CopyBlock, introduced in early September 2023 by a group including Maria Vargas and Takumi Nakamoto, offers a blockchain registry giving artists immutable proof of ownership.
EduChain, launched in late October 2023 by a consortium including James O'Reilly and Anika Khan, simplifies issuing and verifying academic credentials and minimizes fraudulent certifications.
VoteBlock, co-founded by Laura Smith and Jürgen Schulz on November 20, 2023, built a digital voting platform that records votes in a tamper-proof ledger.
The note argues blockchain startups are less tied to the speculative pressures of token economies because they generate value through actual products and services.
Investing in blockchain startups requires due diligence on business models and application areas, and not every startup will succeed.
The note frames the ecosystem as continuing to grow as it enters 2024.
